draft.title: Types of work
card: Full-time
paid work with a set number of hours each week, usually about 38 hours in a standard job. Many full-time jobs are ongoing.
Part-time
paid work with fewer hours than full-time. The hours are usually regular, such as two days a week.
Casual
paid work with no promise of regular hours. The employer can offer shifts when needed, and the worker can often say no.
Unpaid work
work done without a wage. Examples are volunteering for a charity or caring for family members at home. It still helps others and the community.
draft.remember: Work can be paid or unpaid, and paid work differs in how many hours and how regular they are.

a.q: Tom helps at a surf club canteen on Saturdays and gets no wage. What type of work is this?
opts: Unpaid work, because he receives no wage
Casual work, because he works only on Saturdays
Part-time work, because he works fewer hours
Full-time work, because he works every week
a.why: Tom receives no wage, so his work is unpaid, and volunteering is a form of unpaid work. Casual and part-time are tempting because the hours are few, but both of those types are paid work.
a.clue: Is Tom paid for his time?

b.q: Priya works at a Hobart bookshop. She has no set hours, and the manager texts her shifts when the shop is busy. Which type of work is this?
opts: Casual work
Part-time work
Full-time work
Unpaid work
b.why: Priya is paid, but her hours are not regular or promised, which makes her work casual. Part-time work is the tempting answer because her hours are low, but part-time work has regular hours.
b.clue: Look for whether her hours are regular or promised.

a.best: Unpaid work, because he receives no wage

problems.detail: The stem never says Priya is paid, but the why relies on 'Priya is paid'. A bookshop could use volunteers, so stating that she is paid for her shifts would rule out 'Unpaid work' cleanly.
